cosy-lesson.title: Humans May Have Hidden Regenerative Powers

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Regeneration – the process of growing back lost body parts or tissues.

p.em: Example: Lizards are famous for their rapid tail regeneration.

cosy-blockquote.p: Somatic – relating to the physical body rather than the mind.

p.em: Example: Humans have limited somatic healing capabilities.

cosy-blockquote.p: Heal – to become healthy or sound again after an injury.

p.em: Example: Minor cuts on your skin will heal within a few days.

cosy-blockquote.p: Dormant – inactive or sleeping, but capable of becoming active.

p.em: Example: Many desert plants remain dormant during the dry summer.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cell – the smallest structural and functional unit of an organism.

p.em: Example: Our body's stem cells help repair damaged tissue.

cosy-blockquote.p: Active ≠ Passive – engaging or ready to engage in physically energetic pursuits ≠ not active; receiving or submitting to an action without responding.

p.em: Example: The dormant genes became active after the chemical treatment, rather than remaining in a passive state.

cosy-blockquote.p: Trigger – to cause an event or situation to happen or exist.

p.em: Example: Severe injuries trigger a complex healing response.

cosy-blockquote.p: Restore – to return something to its original or former condition.

p.em: Example: The therapy helped restore full movement to his leg.

cosy-blockquote.p: Ability – the physical or mental power to do something.

p.em: Example: Humans lack the ability to grow back entire limbs.

cosy-blockquote.p: Amphibian – a cold-blooded vertebrate animal that can live both in water and on land.

p.em: Example: The axolotl is an amphibian capable of extreme tissue repair.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
According to the article, how does a wild amphibian regrow an entire limb after an amputation?
★ Have you ever had a scar or wound that healed remarkably well over time?

What evidence is presented in the study proving that humans have limited somatic healing powers?
★ Do you find that your body recovers quickly from intense physical exercise or illness?

Based on the research findings, how does a cut on mammalian skin heal itself compared to amphibians?
★ What is your personal approach to helping your body heal when you catch a cold?

According to the paper, what causes certain developmental genes to remain dormant after childhood?
★ Do you find human biology and anatomy fascinating or slightly unsettling?

What data presented in the article shows that a single stem cell can change into multiple tissue types?
★ Have you ever donated blood or tissue? What was the experience like?

According to researchers, how can we make these silent genes active again to repair tissues?
★ How much do you trust modern medicine compared to your body's natural healing?

Based on the text, what specific biochemical signals trigger localized tissue regrowth?
★ What is the most remarkable recovery from injury or illness you have ever witnessed?

What evidence in the paper supports the idea that regenerative therapy can restore lost organ function?
★ Do you believe that a positive mindset can physically speed up biological healing?

How does the study evaluate the human ability to recover from severe heart tissue damage?
★ How often do you think about the biological limits of the human body?

To what extent does the article show that regeneration in vertebrates is controlled by precise genetic networks?
★ What daily habit do you believe contributes most to your physical vitality?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
If future research continues to support this hypothesis (e.g. cellular regeneration theory), humans will recover from amputation through rapid somatic regeneration.
★ Would you undergo genetic therapy to regain lost physical tissues or cartilage?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, regenerative clinics will activate dormant genetic sequences in patients automatically.
★ Do you think extreme biological regeneration would make humans more reckless?

Imagine future research proves that every mammalian cell has a hidden memory of childhood growth, what would doctors do?
★ Should scientists prioritize curing chronic pain over extending the human lifespan?

If future research proves this discovery beyond doubt, we will restore the physical ability to repair heart muscle in senior citizens.
★ Would you want to live in a future where any damaged organ can be printed in a lab?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, targeted chemical compounds will make active healing possible for deep skin burns.
★ Do you think artificial organs will eventually perform better than our biological ones?

Imagine future research shows that we can restore complete sight by growing back retinal tissues, how would society change?
★ How do you think society would change if the human average lifespan reached 150?

If future research continues to support this hypothesis, biological triggers will make somatic decline completely preventable.
★ Would you support the creation of safe synthetic biological enhancements for athletes?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, we will use amphibian cellular matrices to construct organic scaffolding for transplants.
★ Do you think humans will ever lose their natural healing abilities by relying too much on medicine?

Imagine future research proves that minor cuts can heal without leaving any scar tissue, what would this mean for plastic surgery?
★ What is the most important medical breakthrough you hope to see in your lifetime?

If future research continues to support this hypothesis, we will discover the biochemical factors that trigger limb restoration in wild vertebrates.
★ Would you choose to have a minor cosmetic flaw regenerated if it was completely free?

ul.li: Incorrect: The lizards can to regrow tail → Correct: Lizards can regrow their tails ((Can + infinitive without 'to', plural noun))
Incorrect: He was operated last week → Correct: He had an operation last week ((Passive structure vs having an operation))
Incorrect: I am agree with scientifics → Correct: I agree with the scientists ((Agree is a verb, noun 'scientists'))
